name: Firebird
tagline: Lightweight, MVCC relational database from the InterBase lineage, embeddable or client-server.
description: Firebird is an open-source relational database descended from Borland's InterBase 6.0 source release in 2000. It uses a multi-generational (MVCC) architecture, supports stored procedures and triggers in PSQL, and runs either as a server or as an embedded library from the same database file, which made it popular with Delphi and line-of-business desktop software, especially in Brazil, Russia and Europe. Firebird 5 added parallel backup/restore, partial indexes and SQL-level profiling, and the project, run by the Firebird Foundation, ships coordinated patch releases for 3.x, 4.x and 5.x. Firebird 6 is in development, but 5.0 remains the current stable line.

license.name: InterBase Public License / Initial Developer's Public License (MPL-style)

pricing.notes: Free for any use; commercial support from IBSurgeon, IBPhoenix and others.

scale.notes: Single-node; physical and logical replication (since 4.0) for standbys.

strengths: Same engine runs embedded or as a server with no change to the database file
Small footprint and near-zero administration for departmental apps
Readers never block writers thanks to MVCC record versions
Mature PSQL stored procedures, triggers and events
Long-lived stable releases with patches for three major lines
weaknesses: Small ecosystem and few managed hosting options
No native JSON type or full-text search
Garbage collection of old record versions needs attention under long transactions
No built-in sharding or multi-primary clustering
useCases: Embedded databases in point-of-sale or ERP software
